readerSummary: Jamie remains legible as a technical project manager and implementation lead whose operating structures grow from how people gather, contribute, recognize one another, and continue shared work. The About page connects artistic, civic, technical, and social practice directly; WOWList, Sunday Dinner / 196, and NYC Artist Coalition supply distinct, dated continuities. The professional positioning is supported by this lineage rather than displaced by an artist biography.

criteria.evidence: The homepage links to About. criteria.requirement: At least three public-safe project continuities
criteria.evidence: The threeProjectTrace records show organizer participation shaping WOWList, hospitality and artist agency shaping recurring gatherings and residency handoffs, and cultural-space participation shaping coalition web and documentation systems. Historical and present projects are counted in accordance with the owner clarification; dates and status remain explicit.

criteria.requirement: Reader can explain how the systems can be inhabited, influenced, remembered, and continued
criteria.evidence: These systems support people changing the work: organizers use their own vocabulary and maintain their own calendars; residents discuss actual needs and retain agency; coalition collaborators align questions, act through public pathways, and recover decisions through shared memory. Their documentation is a means of continuing social practice.

WOWList names Richard Caceres and organizer labor. Sunday Dinner identifies Julia Fredenburg and Jamie as co-organizers for the 2016 milestone and credits the community. NYC Artist Coalition credits collaborators and disclaims individual causation of policy outcomes. About summarizes Open House's communal governance; no raw article, faculty testimonial, educational record, or private correspondence is reproduced in the reviewed rendered pages or the permitted source note.
